To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exposure to TBT and DBT significantly suppressed Con A-induced mitogenesis in PBMCs from marine mammals and humans at concentrations of up 330 nM, while MBT showed no cytotoxicity at concentrations of up of 3,600 nm.
the immunosuppressive effects of butyltin compounds and non-ortho PCBs were observed in marine mammal lymphocytes in-vitro.
the butyltin compounds suppressed the mitogen-induced proliferation of porpoise, dolphin, seal and human lymphocytes, and the coplanar PCB compounds did not suppress cell mitogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of BTs to suppress the mitogenic response in lymphocytes from Dall's and bottlenose dolphins, a California sea lion, a larga seal and humans.
immunosuppression of marine mammals and humans by exposure to BTs and non-ortho PCBs.
the potential of immunotoxicity caused by BTs and coplantar PCBs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
marine mammals and humans are at risk of immunosuppression by exposure to BTs.
the immunotoxicity of BTs and non-ortho PCBs in marine mammals and humans should be further evaluated in future studies.
the immunotoxicological effects of BTs on the immune system in marine mammals and humans are still unclear and further studies on the immunotoxicity of BTs are required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunotoxicity of BTs in marine mammals is comparable to those in human lymphocytes and the immunosuppressive potency of non-ortho copplanar PCBs is much less than that of BTs.
BTs are more immunotoxic than coplanar PCB congeners in marine mammals.
BTs are a serious concern for the immune functions in marine mammals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

marine mammal lymphocyte responses to mitogens were suppressed by exposure to BTs at concentrations that are found in the liver of free-ranging Dall's porpises, but not by non-ortho coplarar PCBs at concentrations that have been measured in their blubber.
the immunotoxicity of BTs and non-ortho PCBs in marine mammal lymphocytes is similar to that in human lymphocytes.

we have demonstrated that butyltins can cause immune suppression in marine mammals and humans and that the immune suppression can be additive to that caused by non-ortho coplar PCBs, which is a significant new finding.
